methodology: Baseline and optimized token counts derived from static analysis + character-count estimation (1 token ≈ 4 chars). Per-technique savings computed from optimization_log.json. Monthly projection assumes 500 scans/month with 1 full triage pipeline run + 2 interactive agent runs per scan.

notes: Baseline: 89,404 tokens total (58,442 input Sonnet + 20,600 output Sonnet + 8,362 input Haiku + 2,000 output Haiku)
Optimized: 38,213 tokens total after all four techniques applied

input_compression.description: nessus_compressor strips prose/noise, deduplicates CVE+asset pairs, groups by remediation action, aggregates for reports. Applied via compress_for_triage/compress_for_remediation/compress_for_reporting in hakuna/preprocessing/nessus_compressor.py.

prompt_caching.description: Static system prompt block (1300-1936 tokens) marked cache_control=ephemeral. Saves ~80% of system prompt re-billing on steps 2-N of multi-step runs. Implemented in _build_system_prompt_cached() in backend/agent_engine.py.

semantic_caching.description: CVECache (hakuna/cache/cve_cache.py) with 24h TTL for KEV/EPSS, 7d TTL for exploit/threat intel data. Assumes 60% cache hit rate after first scan in a session. Avoids repeated CVE enrichment tool calls across scans.

model_routing.description: ModelRouter (hakuna/routing/model_router.py) routes normalization/ticket_formatting/field_mapping tasks to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. Connectivity tests moved from Sonnet to Haiku. Displaces 8,410 tokens from $3/M to $0.80/M input pricing.

context_management.description: rolling_context() (hakuna/utils/context_manager.py) caps history at 5 turns with 3-turn verbatim tail + summary. CampaignScratchpad provides <500 token state for multi-session campaigns. Primarily benefits agents with max_steps=15-20 (attack_surface, auto_tagger, ticket_creator).

per_agent_breakdown.notes: compress_for_reporting(persona='ciso') provides 90% compression on findings payload — highest single-agent reduction.
Highest steps count means context_management saves most tokens here.
CVE semantic cache has highest impact here — threat_intel calls get_threat_cves repeatedly across scans.
Same tokens, 73% cost reduction from model switch: $3/M → $0.80/M input.

remaining_opportunities: 1. STREAMING OPTIMIZATION: _stream_anthropic uses the same non-streaming create() call; switch to client.messages.stream() context manager to enable true streaming and reduce TTFB — no token savings but better UX.

2. ADAPTIVE MAX_TOKENS: max_tokens=4096 is hardcoded regardless of task. Normalization/extraction stages rarely need > 512 tokens output. Reducing max_tokens for DETERMINISTIC stages would not save billed tokens (output is billed as generated) but prevents runaway responses.

3. TOOL SCHEMA PRUNING: Tool schemas are sent on every step even after an agent has finished calling tools and is composing the final answer. Implement a 'no more tools needed' signal to drop tool schemas from the final 1-2 steps.

4. BATCH CVE ENRICHMENT: threat_intel agent calls get_threat_cves with individual CVE IDs. Batching CVE lookups (N CVEs per call) would reduce total API calls by ~10x and semantic cache lookup overhead.

5. INTER-STAGE HANDOFF COMPRESSION: Pipeline handoffs pass full previous stage output as user_input string. Implement dedicated handoff_compressor() to extract only the structured JSON payload, stripping the surrounding markdown prose.

6. EXTENDED PROMPT CACHE TTL: Anthropic ephemeral cache TTL is 5 minutes. For agents run within the same session, cache warm-up pays off on steps 2+. Consider scheduling batch analysis runs to maximize cache hit rate across multiple scans.

7. SCRATCHPAD INJECTION EVERYWHERE: CampaignScratchpad is available but not yet wired into campaign_builder or ticket_creator agent flows. Wiring it in would remove the need to re-fetch campaign state from DB on each step.
